thread.title: Cornell women prepare for Ivy League outdoor track and field championships

author: h. j. hinton
title: Cornell women prepare for Ivy League outdoor track and field championships
text:
The Cornell Big Red women’s outdoor track and field team will compete at the Ivy League Heptagonal Outdoor Track & Field Championships at Princeton University on May 16-17.
The event brings together top athletes from across the Ivy League to compete for conference titles. Cornell enters with strong performances in multiple events, aiming to finish near the top of the team standings.
Avery Hilliard leads Cornell as the defending Ivy League pole vault champion. She holds the school record in that event and is ranked third in the conference this season, as well as among the top 70 nationally. Paula-Marie Brown is another key contributor, ranking second in both heptathlon and high jump within the league, fifth in long jump, and No. 62 nationally in heptathlon.
Cornell’s sprint group has also shown promise: Natasha Redmond ranks fifth in the league for 100 meters, while Arianna Allen and Divine Bamgboye are among the top seven in 100-meter hurdles. The Big Red’s relay teams are also competitive, with their 4×100 squad ranked fifth.
In distance events, Mairead Clas is sixth in the league for 5,000 meters after recording one of Cornell’s fastest times ever this spring. In field events such as hammer throw and shot put, Avery Hastings (second), Nicole Loy (sixth), and Claire Springer (tenth) contribute valuable points.
Freshman Sophia Comfere has made an immediate impact by setting program records for first-year athletes in both 400m and 800m races this spring. The close connection between men’s and women’s teams at Cornell has fostered a supportive environment throughout their season.
With favorable weather forecasted during championship weekend at Princeton, Cornell looks to build on its momentum against strong competition.
